skill.description: Guides agents in building renderable HyperFrames HTML video projects with correct timing attributes, tracks, sub-compositions, variables, media placement, deterministic animation, Tailwind, and validation.

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code spans, template literals, and DOM identifiers. Confirmed issues include third-party CDN scripts, unpinned npx commands, persistent worker files, and a headless CLI path that bypasses delegation consent. The consent bypass should block publication until removed.

remediation.issue: The fallback uses headless Codex workers when the user has not granted delegation.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user consent before every worker path. Without consent, use inline serial execution and do not start headless CLI children.

remediation.issue: Worker prompts and logs can persist full dispatch context on disk.
remediation.suggestion: Minimize copied context, store files in a restricted temporary directory, redact secrets, and delete prompt and log artifacts after collection.

remediation.issue: Validation and render guidance uses unpinned npx package execution.
remediation.suggestion: Pin the HyperFrames package version, prefer a lockfile or trusted local installation, and request approval before executing commands.

remediation.issue: Composition examples load executable GSAP code from a third-party CDN without integrity metadata.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle the dependency locally. If a CDN is required, pin the version and add verified integrity and crossorigin attributes.

content.value_statement: HTML video projects can fail because timing, layout, media, and sub-composition contracts are easy to violate. This skill guides agents through correct HyperFrames structure, deterministic animation, planning, and validation.
actual_capabilities: Selects monolithic or modular composition structures based on scene boundaries and shared state.
Defines composition roots, clips, timing attributes, track indexes, and relative timing.
Wires sub-composition templates, host identifiers, scoped styles, and timeline registry keys.
Configures variables, media placement, volume, source binding, and per-instance overrides.
Applies deterministic GSAP and Tailwind v4 rules for seekable video rendering.
Provides storyboard, narration script, validation, snapshot, preview, and render guidance.
limitations: It documents the HyperFrames contract but does not replace detailed animation, media, creative, registry, or CLI skills.
It does not render video without a compatible HyperFrames project and CLI environment.
Some examples load third-party browser scripts and require network access unless dependencies are bundled locally.
Validation commands can miss cross-file mount, layout, and final visual problems, so snapshot review remains necessary.

output_examples.input: Plan a five-second title card for a product announcement.
output: A standalone 1920 by 1080 composition with one five-second visual clip.
A paused timeline reveals the title and subtitle from explicit starting states.
The plan includes lint, validation, inspection, snapshot, and preview checks.

output_examples.input: Split a thirty-second video into intro, body, and outro scenes.
output: A thin host composition with three sequential sub-composition slots.
Each slot uses matching host, root, and timeline identifiers.
Continuous audio remains a direct child of the host root on a separate track.

output_examples.input: Find why a sub-composition looks correct in preview but loses styles during render.
output_examples.output: The review identifies styles outside the template or root styles keyed by a class. It recommends moving styles inside and targeting the root identifier.

best_practices: Build the final static layout first, then animate explicit states on one paused, registered timeline.
Keep media as direct host-root children and verify cross-file identifiers before validation.
Use snapshots and visual review because static checks cannot detect every assembled-render failure.
anti_patterns: Do not use clocks, unseeded randomness, input state, infinite loops, or render-time asset fetches for visual state.
Do not place required sub-composition styles, scripts, or markup outside the template.
Do not run unpinned external commands or spawn background workers without explicit user approval.

faq.question: What does this skill build?
faq.answer: It guides the structure and validation of HTML projects that HyperFrames can seek and render as video.

faq.question: Does it support sub-compositions?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers host slots, templates, matching identifiers, scoped styles, independent timelines, and per-instance variables.

faq.question: Can I use Tailwind?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance targets the scaffolded Tailwind v4 browser runtime and recommends static class tokens.

faq.question: Where should video and audio elements live?
faq.answer: They should be direct children of the host composition root. Sub-composition templates should contain visual frames and overlays.

faq.question: Why can preview differ from the final render?
faq.answer: Preview may not expose CSS scoping, cross-file identifiers, media discovery, frame-zero readiness, or composited background problems.

faq.question: Does the skill run validation automatically?
faq.answer: It provides validation commands and completion gates. Command execution still requires an available CLI and appropriate user approval.
